title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-util-reporting-ci-fix
author: Priya Patel
description:
Motivation: Recent rollout of the dedicated autoscaler burst controls (ENG-2143) exposed a flaky CI failure in the token-bucket smoothing e2e test and a race condition in the backpressure metric collector. This PR fixes the CI flakiness and hardens utilization reporting for the fleet autoscaler.

Summary: single PR that includes: (1) a deterministic test harness for token-bucket smoothing e2e tests, (2) a synchronization fix in the fleet utilization collector to avoid data races under high concurrency, (3) additional telemetry (backpressure_events counter, per-fleet throughput_guarantee_violation gauge) and (4) a CI pipeline tweak to run the dedicated e2e job against a stable fixture. Key goals: reduce CI flakiness, improve accuracy of utilization reports used by capacity billing and autoscaler decisions, and avoid transient regressions during canary rollouts.

Checklist:
- [x] Reproduce flaky e2e locally and in CI
- [x] Fix race in utilization collector
- [x] Add unit and e2e tests (deterministic harness)
- [x] Add metrics and dashboards notes
- [x] Update release notes and changelog

Testing and results: Unit and e2e run on CI: earlier failure rate ~12% for token-bucket smoothing e2e; after changes the job is stable in 20 successive CI runs. Local microbenchmarks show <1% overhead for the synchronization path, and utilization accuracy improved on synthetic workload by reducing under-reporting during burst periods (median delta from ground truth reduced from 7.3% to 1.1%).

Rollout: feature gated behind rollout flag dedicated.autoscaler.burst_smoothing_v2, default off for 48 hours post-merge for gradual canaries. If regressions observed, automatic rollback via route policy to previous autoscaler implementation (handled by runtime fallback).
